summary: When someone sends a shaliach and forgot the item was hekdesh: if the shaliach did what he was told, the owner did me'ilah, but if the shaliach changed the job, the shaliach did me'ilah.

chunks.en: A shaliach who did his job,
chunks.st: With regard to an agent who performed his agency properly,
chunks.stMore: if he was tasked to make use of a particular item, and the one who appointed him forgot that it was a consecrated item,

words.note: A messenger sent to do something for someone else.

chunks.en: the owner did me'ilah.
chunks.st: the homeowner, who appointed him, is liable for misuse
chunks.stMore: of the consecrated item, as the agent acted on his behalf. Contrary to other cases of agency, where the guiding principle is that there is no agency in the performance of a transgression, and the agent is liable, in this case there is agency, and the homeowner is liable for the action of the agent.

words.note: Me'ilah is using something that belongs to the Beis HaMikdash for yourself.

chunks.en: If he did not do his job,
chunks.st: But if he did not perform his agency

chunks.en: the shaliach did me'ilah.
chunks.st: the agent is liable for misuse
chunks.stMore: of the consecrated item, as once the agent deviates from his agency, he ceases to be an agent, and his actions are attributable to him.

chunks.en: How? If the owner said to him,
chunks.st: How so? If the homeowner said to the agent:

chunks.he: תֵּן בָּשָׂר לָאוֹרְחִים וְנָתַן לָהֶם כָּבֵד,
chunks.en: Give meat to the guests, and he gave them liver,
chunks.st: Give meat to the guests, and he gave them liver;

chunks.en: or liver, and he gave them meat,
chunks.st: or if he said: Give them liver, and he gave them meat,

chunks.en: the shaliach did me'ilah.
chunks.st: the agent is liable for misuse
chunks.stMore: of the consecrated item, as he deviated from his agency.

chunks.en: If he said to him,
chunks.st: If the homeowner said to the agent:

chunks.en: Give them one piece each,
chunks.st: Give them meat, a piece for this guest and a piece for that guest,

chunks.en: and he said, Take two each,
chunks.st: and the agent says: Each of you take two pieces,

chunks.en: and they took three each,
chunks.st: and each of the guests took three pieces,

chunks.en: all of them did me'ilah.
chunks.st: all of them are liable for misuse.
chunks.stMore: The homeowner is liable for their consumption of the first piece of meat, as with regard to that piece his instructions were fulfilled. The agent is liable for the second piece, which he added to the instructions of the homeowner. Finally, the guests are liable for the third piece, which they took at their own initiative beyond the instructions of the agent.

chunks.en: If he said to him,
chunks.st: If the homeowner said to the agent:

chunks.he: הָבֵא לִי מִן הַחַלּוֹן אוֹ מִגְּלֻסְקְמָא,
chunks.en: Bring me from the window or from the box,
chunks.st: Bring me this item or this money from the window in the wall or from the chest [hadeluskema],

chunks.en: and he brought it to him,
chunks.st: and the agent obeyed and brought it to him from the place that he instructed him,

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמַר בַּעַל הַבַּיִת
chunks.en: even though the owner said,
chunks.st: even though the homeowner said:

chunks.en: I only meant from that place,
chunks.st: In my heart, my desire was only that he should bring me the item from that other place,

chunks.en: and he brought it from this place,
chunks.st: and as he brought it from this place he did not fulfill my instructions,

chunks.en: the owner did me'ilah.
chunks.st: nevertheless the homeowner is liable for misuse
chunks.stMore: if the item or money is consecrated, as the agent did in fact fulfill his instructions.

chunks.en: But if he said to him,
chunks.st: But if the homeowner said to the agent:

chunks.en: Bring me from the window,
chunks.st: Bring me this item or this money from the window in the wall,

chunks.en: and he brought it to him from the box,
chunks.st: and the agent brought it to him from the chest;

chunks.he: אוֹ מִן גְּלֻסְקְמָא וְהֵבִיא לוֹ מִן הַחַלּוֹן,
chunks.en: or from the box, and he brought it to him from the window,
chunks.st: or if the homeowner said to the agent: Bring me this item or this money from the chest, and the agent brought it to him from the window,

chunks.en: the shaliach did me'ilah.
chunks.st: the agent is liable for misuse.

summary: If someone sent hekdesh money with someone who cannot be a shaliach, or remembered it was hekdesh too late, the storekeeper may be the one who does me'ilah. The owner can fix it by switching the holiness onto another coin or kli.

chunks.en: If he sent it with a cheresh,
chunks.st: In a case where the homeowner sent consecrated money in the hand of a deaf-mute,

words.note: Someone who cannot hear or speak.

chunks.en: a shoteh, or a child,
chunks.st: an imbecile, or a minor,
chunks.stMore: who lack halakhic competence and cannot be commissioned as agents, in order to purchase an item from a storekeeper,

words.note: Someone who cannot think clearly for himself.

chunks.en: if they did his job,
chunks.st: if they performed his agency,

chunks.en: the owner did me'ilah.
chunks.st: the homeowner is liable for misuse,

chunks.en: If they did not do his job,
chunks.st: If they did not perform his agency
chunks.stMore: but purchased a different item from the storekeeper,

chunks.en: the storekeeper did me'ilah.
chunks.st: the storekeeper is liable for misuse.

chunks.en: If he sent it with a grown-up who understands,
chunks.st: If the homeowner sent the money in the hand of a halakhically competent person

chunks.he: וְנִזְכַּר עַד שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ אֵצֶל הַחֶנְוָנִי,
chunks.en: and he remembered before the shaliach got to the storekeeper,
chunks.st: and the homeowner remembered that the money was consecrated before the agent reached the storekeeper,

chunks.en: the storekeeper does me'ilah when he spends it.
chunks.st: the storekeeper is liable for misuse when he spends
chunks.stMore: the money for his personal use. The homeowner is exempt from liability for misuse, because once he remembers that the money is consecrated his misuse is no longer unwitting, and one is liable to bring an offering for misuse only for unwitting misuse of consecrated property.

chunks.en: What should he do?
chunks.st: What shall the homeowner do in a case where he remembers that the money is consecrated, in order to prevent the storekeeper from liability for misuse?

chunks.en: He takes a perutah or a kli and says,
chunks.st: He takes one peruta or a vessel and says:

chunks.he: פְּרוּטָה שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁהִיא,
chunks.en: The perutah of hekdesh, wherever it is,
chunks.st: The consecrated peruta, wherever it may be,

words.note: Hekdesh means things that belong to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: is switched onto this one,
chunks.explain: Its holiness moves onto this coin or kli.
chunks.st: is desacralized with this peruta or vessel.

chunks.en: because hekdesh can be redeemed with money or with something worth money.
chunks.st: as a consecrated item is desacralized with money and with an item that has the equivalent value of money. The result is that the storekeeper spends non-sacred money.

summary: A shaliach was given a hekdesh perutah to buy lamps and wicks. If he changed only half the job, neither does me'ilah, but if he bought from the wrong stores, he changed it all and he does me'ilah.

chunks.en: If he gave him a perutah,
chunks.st: If the homeowner gave the agent one consecrated peruta

chunks.en: and said to him,
chunks.st: and said to him:

chunks.he: הָבֵא לִי בְחֶצְיָהּ נֵרוֹת וּבְחֶצְיָהּ פְּתִילוֹת,
chunks.en: Bring me lamps with half and wicks with half,
chunks.st: Bring me lamps [nerot] with one-half of it and wicks with one-half of it,

chunks.en: and he went and brought him, with all of it,
chunks.st: and the agent went and brought him wicks with the entire

chunks.en: lamps, or with all of it wicks,
chunks.st: peruta, or lamps with the entire peruta;

chunks.en: or if he said to him,
chunks.st: or in a case where the homeowner said to the agent:

chunks.en: Bring me lamps with all of it
chunks.st: Bring me lamps with the entire peruta

chunks.en: or wicks with all of it,
chunks.st: or wicks with the entire peruta,

chunks.en: and he went and brought him with half
chunks.st: and the agent went and brought him

chunks.en: lamps and with half wicks,
chunks.st: lamps with one-half of it and wicks with one-half of it,

chunks.en: neither of them did me'ilah.
chunks.st: both of them are not liable for misuse of the peruta.
chunks.stMore: In both cases, the homeowner is exempt because his instructions were fulfilled only with regard to half of a peruta, and the agent is exempt as he spent only half of a peruta on his own initiative.

chunks.en: But if he said to him,
chunks.st: But if the homeowner said to the agent:

chunks.en: Bring me lamps with half from such a place
chunks.st: Bring me lamps from such and such place with one-half of

chunks.en: and wicks with half from such a place,
chunks.st: the peruta and wicks from such and such place with one-half of the peruta,

chunks.en: and he went and brought him lamps from the wick store
chunks.st: and the agent went and brought him lamps from the place that he designated for

chunks.en: and wicks from the lamp store,
chunks.st: wicks, and wicks from the place that he designated for lamps,

chunks.en: the shaliach did me'ilah.
chunks.st: the agent is liable for misuse, as he deviated from the homeowner’s instructions by the sum of an entire peruta.

summary: A shaliach was sent to buy one esrog but bought an esrog and a pomegranate. The Tanna Kamma says both did me'ilah; Rabbi Yehudah says the owner did not, because he wanted one big esrog. The same goes for a robe.

chunks.en: If he gave him two perutos,
chunks.st: If the homeowner gave the agent two consecrated perutot,

chunks.en: and said to him,
chunks.st: and said to him:

chunks.en: Bring me an esrog,
chunks.st: Go and bring me an etrog,

chunks.en: and he went and brought him with one perutah
chunks.st: and he went and brought him

chunks.en: an esrog, and with one perutah a pomegranate,
chunks.st: an etrog with one peruta and a pomegranate with one peruta,

chunks.en: both of them did me'ilah.
chunks.st: both of them are liable for misuse.
chunks.stMore: The homeowner is liable because his agency was performed with the sum of one peruta, and the agent is liable because he deviated from the homeowner’s instructions with one peruta.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: the owner did not do me'ilah,
chunks.st: The homeowner is not liable for misuse,

chunks.en: because he can say to him,
chunks.st: as he can say to the agent:

chunks.en: I wanted a big esrog,
chunks.st: I was seeking a large etrog worth two perutot,

chunks.en: and you brought me a small, bad one.
chunks.st: and you brought me a small, inferior etrog worth one peruta.

chunks.en: If he gave him a gold dinar,
chunks.st: If the homeowner gave the agent a consecrated gold dinar,
chunks.stMore: which is worth twenty-five silver dinars, as four silver dinars constitute a sela;

chunks.en: and said to him, Bring me a robe,
chunks.st: and said to the agent: Go and bring me a robe,

chunks.en: and he went and brought him with three
chunks.st: and the agent went and brought him

chunks.en: a robe, and with three a tallis,
chunks.st: a robe with three sela and a cloak with three sela,

chunks.en: both of them did me'ilah.
chunks.st: both of them are liable for misuse.
chunks.stMore: The homeowner is liable because his agency was performed with the purchase of the robe for three sela, and the agent is liable because he deviated from the homeowner’s instructions by purchasing the cloak.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: the owner did not do me'ilah,
chunks.st: The homeowner is not liable for misuse,

chunks.en: because he can say to him,
chunks.st: as he can say to the agent:

chunks.en: I wanted a big robe,
chunks.st: I was seeking a large robe worth a gold dinar

chunks.en: and you brought me a small, bad one.
chunks.st: and you brought me a small, inferior robe worth three sela, i.e., twelve silver dinars.

summary: If hekdesh money was left with a money changer, he may use it if it was not tied up, so spending it is not me'ilah. If it was left with a regular person, he may not use it either way. Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehudah argue about a storekeeper.

chunks.en: Someone who leaves money with a money changer,
chunks.st: With regard to one who deposits consecrated money with a money changer,

words.note: A shulchani: a person who changes coins and keeps money, like a bank.

chunks.en: if it is tied up,
chunks.st: if the money is bound,

chunks.en: he may not use it.
chunks.st: the money changer may not use it.

chunks.en: So if he spent it, he did me'ilah.
chunks.st: Therefore, if the money changer spent the money, he is liable for its misuse.

chunks.en: If it is loose,
chunks.st: If the money was unbound

chunks.en: he may use it.
chunks.st: he may use it,

chunks.en: So if he spent it,
chunks.st: and therefore if the money changer spent the money,

chunks.en: he did not do me'ilah.
chunks.st: he is not liable for its misuse.

chunks.en: With a regular person,
chunks.st: By contrast, if one deposited money with a homeowner,

chunks.en: either way,
chunks.st: whether it is bound or whether it is unbound,

chunks.en: he may not use it.
chunks.st: the one with whom it was deposited may not use it,

chunks.en: So if he spent it, he did me'ilah.
chunks.st: and therefore if he spent the money, he is liable for misuse.

chunks.en: A storekeeper is like a regular person,
chunks.st: In this regard, the halakhic status of a storekeeper is like that of a homeowner;

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says, like a money changer.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: The halakhic status of a storekeeper is like that of a money changer.

summary: A perutah of hekdesh got mixed into a purse of coins. Rabbi Akiva says spending the first coin is me'ilah; the Chachamim say only after spending all of them. Rabbi Akiva agrees when someone said "a perutah from this purse."

chunks.he: פְּרוּטָה שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁנָּפְלָה לְתוֹךְ הַכִּיס,
chunks.en: A perutah of hekdesh that fell into a purse,
chunks.st: If a consecrated peruta fell into one’s purse,
chunks.stMore: in which there were non-sacred perutot,

chunks.en: or if he said,
chunks.st: or in a case where one said:

chunks.en: A perutah in this purse is hekdesh,
chunks.st: One peruta in this purse is consecrated,

chunks.en: once he spent the first one, he did me'ilah.
chunks.st: once he spent the first peruta from the purse for non-sacred purposes, he is liable for its misuse.

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Akiva.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: And the Chachamim say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: not until he spends the whole purse.
chunks.st: He is not liable for misuse until he spends all the perutot in the entire purse,
chunks.stMore: as only then is it certain that he spent the consecrated peruta.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva agrees if someone says, A perutah
chunks.st: And Rabbi Akiva concedes to the Rabbis in a case where one says: One peruta from

chunks.en: from this purse is hekdesh,
chunks.st: the coins in this purse is consecrated,

chunks.en: that he may keep spending until
chunks.st: that he may continue spending the perutot in the purse for non-sacred purposes and becomes liable for misuse only

chunks.en: he spends the whole purse.
chunks.st: once he spends all the perutot in the entire purse.
chunks.stMore: His formulation indicates that his desire was that the final remaining peruta in the purse would be consecrated, and therefore one is liable for misuse only when he spends that peruta.
